beats.narration_text: Someone assumed Claude would watch their competitors continuously, like a monitoring service. It doesn't — it researches on request, following one fixed recipe. So: can Claude research my competitors for me?

beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it works. This one is competitive-intelligence — research your competitors, then build an interactive battlecard. The SKILL.md holds that whole instruction set, plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.

Ask with a phrase like 'battlecard for one competitor' or 'how do we compare to them,' and the pipeline runs: read the trigger, research each competitor named, then build one HTML artifact — clickable competitor cards, plus a comparison matrix. Claude works through the steps in order. Linear — no branching unless a step says so.

That's the whole job, not open-ended monitoring: research the competitors you named, build that one battlecard, then stop. Ask for a rival that's not on your list, or a shape besides the battlecard, and there's nothing to fall back on — the spec only produces what's written into it.
A skill runs the same recipe on the same request every time — the same battlecard, never more than what the file says to build.

props.quote: A skill runs the same recipe on the same request every time — the same battlecard, never more than what the file says to build.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Read the competitive-intelligence skill and walk me through what you'll do before you do it. Then run it for one real competitor of mine. Check what comes back: is it the same two things every time — the battlecard's cards and its comparison matrix — or did it wander outside the spec?
